Mark the student's response to a question from the 2018 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 23(c) [6 marks]: How would the situational analysis change if the business decides to expand into Europe?
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
A manufacturing business has conducted a situational analysis and determined the following:
• It has loyal customers who make repeat purchases.
• The size of the Australian market is shrinking.
• Some staff need further training to use the factory machinery.
• The owner has been invited to invest in similar factories in Europe.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 6):
6 marks: Clearly shows how the situational analysis will change if the business expands into Europe
5 marks: Shows how the situational analysis will change if the business expands into Europe
3–4 marks: Provides characteristics and features of a changed situational analysis if the business expands into Europe
2 marks: Sketches in general terms feature/s of a changed situational analysis
1 marks: Recognises and names a feature of a situational analysis

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
A strength will no longer be that the business has loyal customers as it is unknown in the European market. Instead, a strength could be experience in the manufacturing business in the Australian market. The weakness will change from 'some staff need further training to use factory machinery' to 'all European employees involved in manufacturing will need training in the use of factory machinery'. Additionally, there is a lack of knowledge of the European market. The opportunity will change from 'the owner has been invited to invest in similar factories in Europe' to 'possible expansion or consolidation to more areas in Europe'. The threat of the shrinking Australian market may change to a new threat from established businesses operating in Europe.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: identify a threat to the business (a)
Better responses: demonstrate an understanding of monitoring and controlling by providing characteristics and features of this component of the marketing process (b)
Better responses: link the action of monitoring and controlling due to the business expansion to an element of the marketing process (b)
Better responses: acknowledge the original position of the situational analysis and the changed position as a result of the business expansion (c)
Better responses: consistently refer to the changing components of the situational analysis as a result of the expansion (c).
To improve: providing features of monitoring and controlling, and relating them to the changed situational analysis (b)
To improve: providing features of a changing situational analysis using business terminology with application to the stimulus (c).

STUDENT RESPONSE:
